items.title: 2026 Federal Budget officially tabled — CGT and negative gearing changes confirmed
items.summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers has officially tabled the 2026 Federal Budget. The 50% CGT discount is abolished from 1 July 2027, replaced by CPI indexation plus a hard 30% minimum tax floor on net capital gains.

items.title: Grandfathering explained: Which property investors keep their tax breaks
items.summary: Properties purchased before Budget Night (7:30 PM, 13 May 2026) or new builds remain fully exempt. Existing properties bought after Budget Night lose negative gearing offsets against salary income.

items.title: Pre-1985 share holdings: ATO valuation reset confirmed for 1 July 2027
items.summary: Shares purchased before 20 September 1985 will have their cost base reset via ATO market valuation on 1 July 2027, ending the 42-year legacy CGT exemption.

items.title: Economists warn 30% minimum CGT floor will push retirees into higher tax brackets
items.summary: Several economists have raised concerns that the strict 30% minimum tax floor will disproportionately impact retirees who historically timed asset sales to minimise tax in lower-income years.

items.title: SMSFs confirmed exempt: Retain one-third CGT discount under new rules
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed Self-Managed Superannuation Funds are completely excluded from the CGT discount removal. SMSFs retain their existing one-third discount, maintaining a significant tax advantage.

items.title: New builds remain fully exempt — developer lobby claims budget favours supply
items.summary: Newly constructed residential properties are exempt from both the negative gearing and CGT changes. Property developer lobbies say this is a deliberate policy to encourage housing supply.

items.title: Opposition flags Senate challenge — legislation not yet passed into law
items.summary: The Coalition has flagged it will challenge key provisions of the CGT and negative gearing changes in the Senate. These measures are not yet law and must pass both houses of parliament.

items.title: Budget Night: Full text of Treasurer's speech released
items.summary: The full transcript of Treasurer Chalmers' Budget Night address is available. Key tax changes take effect 1 July 2027, with a grandfathering cut-off of 7:30 PM on 13 May 2026.

items.title: Division 296 super tax: $3m threshold applies from 1 July 2026
items.summary: Division 296 legislation was passed in March 2026 and will commence from 1 July 2026, introducing an additional 15% tax on superannuation earnings for accounts exceeding $3 million. The new tax affects both SMSF and APRA-regulated fund members with balances above this threshold, representing a significant change for high-balance superannuation accounts.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform flagged — Government indicates plan to shift burden from income to assets
items.summary: The 2026 Budget signals potential reforms to the tax treatment of trusts, with the Government indicating a broader shift away from taxing incomes towards taxing assets. Labor has stated the plan aims to rebalance the tax system by targeting distribution arrangements commonly used by high-net-worth individuals to minimise tax on investment earnings.

items.title: Senate referral: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has been referred to the Senate Economics Legislation Committee for inquiry and report.

items.title: Foreign Resident Notification Legislation Pending
items.summary: The government has again deferred the commencement date for provisions requiring foreign residents disposing of shares and membership interests exceeding $50m to notify the ATO before executing transactions. Legislation remains pending parliamentary passage. This represents a recurring deferral that has been noted in prior years per Grant Thornton analysis.

items.title: Division 296 high-balance super tax ($3 m threshold) commences 1 July 2026 per enacted legislation
items.summary: The Better Targeted Super Concessions Act 2026 received Royal Assent on 20 March 2026, introducing Division 296 which imposes a 15% tax on superannuation earnings above the $3m threshold. Starting 1 July 2026, individuals with total superannuation balances exceeding $3m will be subject to this additional tax on their earnings. The ATO will administer the new tax regime through the existing superannuation system.

items.title: Division 296 super tax: indexed thresholds and CGT relief confirmed
items.summary: Treasury has released draft legislation for Division 296, introducing indexed thresholds and capital gains tax (CGT) relief provisions for superannuation funds. The Australian Taxation Office confirms the legislation is enacted and will commence from 1 July 2026, affecting individuals with super balances exceeding $3 Million. This represents a significant update to Australia's superannuation tax framework.

items.title: Correction: Negative Gearing and CGT Changes Apply from Budget Night
items.summary: The government's changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax (CGT) apply to properties purchased after 7:30pm on 12 May 2026 (budget night), not 13 May 2026 as previously stated. Properties purchased before this deadline remain subject to existing negative gearing rules. Investors and home buyers should note this one-day difference when timing property purchases.

items.title: Budget 2026: Negative gearing restrictions introduced for established properties
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget introduces restrictions on negative gearing for established property investments. Purchases of established properties after 7:30pm on 12 May 2026 will not be eligible for negative gearing deductions, with the change effective from 1 July 2027. Newly constructed homes remain eligible, reflecting the government's strategy to increase housing supply through investor activity in new builds.

items.title: Negative gearing reform reverses earlier election promise
items.summary: The negative gearing changes represent a significant policy reversal for the government, which previously indicated it would not restrict negative gearing. The reform builds on capital gains tax changes already legislated for properties purchased after 14 May 2024, creating a broader shift in property investment taxation. Property investors purchasing established homes from mid-2027 onwards will face reduced tax benefits compared to previous arrangements.

items.title: Federal Budget 2026-27: What It Means for Australian Investors
items.summary: The site previously stated the cutoff for capital gains tax changes was 13 May 2026, but the correct cutoff is 7:30pm on 12 May 2026 (budget night).

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT changes affect ETF and Listed Investment Vehicle investors
items.summary: ASX published analysis on how the capital gains tax changes will affect investors in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and Listed Investment Vehicles (LIVs). The analysis considers the practical implications for retail investors holding these products through the tax changes, providing guidance on how the 2026 Federal Budget measures may impact their portfolio returns and tax obligations.

items.title: ASX analysis details CGT impact on ETFs and Listed Investment Vehicles
items.summary: The ASX has published specific guidance for investors in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and Listed Investment Vehicles (LIVs) addressing how the proposed CGT changes differ from those affecting direct property and share investments. The update clarifies the treatment of reinvested dividends and managed fund conversions for retail investors holding these products through superannuation or non-superannuation accounts.

items.title: Budget allocates $47.5m to Treasury and ATO for CGT reform implementation
items.summary: The government will provide $47.5 million over four years (with $3.9 million per year ongoing) to fund Treasury and ATO implementation of the capital gains tax changes. This represents a significant administrative investment in the CGT reform rollout. The funding demonstrates the government's commitment to ensuring effective implementation of the tax changes.

items.title: ASA calls for capital gains averaging alongside indexation reform
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association has publicly responded to the capital gains tax changes, calling for an averaging mechanism to address income bunching where gains realised in a single tax year could push investors into higher brackets. The ASA warned that the changes may cause significant issues for investors who hold assets for many years, and stated they preferred proper consultation before the changes were announced.

items.title: Budget confirms minimum 30% tax on capital gains from July 2027
items.summary: The official Budget website confirms the Government will introduce a minimum 30% tax on capital gains, replacing the 50% CGT discount with inflation-based indexation from 1 July 2027. This reform represents a significant shift in how capital gains are taxed in Australia, affecting investors and property owners. The change will apply to assets acquired after the implementation date.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis has quantified that inflation accounted for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade, providing crucial context for the government's proposed CGT indexation reforms. This data underpins the rationale for replacing the flat 50% CGT discount with inflation indexation, suggesting a significant portion of historical share price growth was illusory nominal appreciation rather than real returns.

items.title: Pre-budget announcement: Trust tax treatment reform flagged as Government signals shift from income to asset taxation
items.summary: The Government has flagged significant reforms to trust tax treatment, signaling a fundamental shift from taxing income to taxing assets. The Treasurer indicated the plan would rebalance the tax system, moving away from income-based taxation. This reform forms part of broader tax changes announced alongside CGT adjustments and negative gearing restrictions in Budget 2026-27.

items.title: Working Australians Tax Offset: $250 annual relief confirmed for low-to-middle income workers
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget introduces a new Working Australians Tax Offset providing $250 annual tax relief for eligible workers earning approximately $20,000 to $67,000. The offset will be delivered through adjustments to tax withholding from 1 July 2026, reducing the tax burden for around 4 million low-to-middle income earners.

items.title: Foreign resident capital gains notification threshold remains at $50m
items.summary: Foreign residents disposing of shares and membership interests exceeding $50 million in value must notify the ATO before executing the transaction. The commencement date for these provisions has again been deferred until the legislation passes Parliament. Taxpayers should ensure compliance procedures are in place pending the legislative update.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis shows inflation accounted for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade, providing key data for the government's rationale to replace the flat 50% CGT discount with inflation indexation. The analysis underpins the government's claim that the existing 50% discount overcompensates investors for inflationary gains rather than genuine economic growth. This data has been cited as central justification for the proposed CGT reform in the 2026 budget.

items.title: Division 296 super tax: indexed thresholds and CGT relief details confirmed by ATO
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed that Division 296 tax commences on 1 July 2026, introducing a 15% tax on superannuation earnings above the $3 million balance threshold. The agency has also clarified indexed threshold arrangements and confirmed capital gains tax (CGT) relief provisions for affected self-managed superannuation funds (SMSFs), providing certainty for trustees navigating the new requirements.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis underpinning the CGT reform has found that inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade. This finding provides important context for why the government chose indexation-based reform rather than simple rate changes. The analysis supports the rationale that a significant portion of nominal capital gains are attributable to inflationary pressures rather than real value creation.

items.title: Foreign resident capital gains notification legislation deferred again
items.summary: Foreign resident capital gains notification requirements for disposals exceeding $50m have been deferred again, with commencement now dependent on legislation passing Parliament. The requirement would have obligated foreign residents disposing of shares and membership interests to notify the ATO before executing transactions. This marks another deferral of the measure, which was originally announced in the 2020-21 Budget.

items.title: Treasury analysis quantifies inflation impact on ASX 200 share gains
items.summary: Treasury analysis has found that inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade, providing significant economic context for the Capital Gains Tax indexation reforms. The analysis highlights how nominal investment returns have been substantially inflated by general price increases rather than genuine wealth creation. This finding comes as the government proceeds with CGT indexation changes that will link gains to inflation-adjusted measures.

items.title: Treasury modelling: inflation accounted for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis published in the budget papers reveals that inflation accounted for 56% of asset price growth for ASX 200 shares held over the 10 years to March 2026. This empirical finding provides the basis for the government's proposal to replace the capital gains tax discount with inflation indexation. The modelling demonstrates that more than half of historical share gains can be attributed to inflationary pressures rather than real economic growth.

items.title: ATO confirms Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details
items.summary: The ATO has published guidance on Division 296 tax including indexed thresholds for the $3m balance threshold, methodology for calculating earnings on Total Superannuation Balance exceeding the threshold, and CGT relief provisions for SMSFs. The legislation was enacted in March 2026 and commences 1 July 2026. This provides definitive administrative guidance for affected super fund members.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis published in Budget 2026–27 documentation has quantified that approximately 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade were attributable to inflationary effects rather than real economic growth. This data provides the quantitative foundation for the government's proposed CGT reform, replacing the 50% discount with inflation indexation to ensure only genuine capital gains are subject to tax.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform flagged — Government signals plan to shift burden from income to assets
items.summary: The 2026 Budget indicates the Government plans to reform trust tax treatment, shifting the burden away from taxing income and more towards taxing assets. This follows similar moves on negative gearing and CGT, forming part of a broader tax system rebalancing according to Treasurer Jim Chalmers. Details of the reform framework are expected to be released in coming months.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expansion confirmed from July 2027
items.summary: The 2026 Federal Budget confirms the expansion of venture capital tax incentives, with new settings commencing from 1 July 2027. This measure forms part of the broader tax reform agenda aimed at boosting investment in innovation and startups across Australia. The government expects the enhanced incentives to attract greater private capital to early-stage businesses and grow the startup ecosystem.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform signals shift from income to asset taxation
items.summary: The Government has signalled plans to reform trust tax treatment, shifting the burden from taxing incomes to taxing assets as part of broader tax reform. The changes would work alongside proposed alterations to capital gains tax (CGT) and negative gearing policies. This represents a fundamental change in how investment structures are taxed in Australia.

items.title: CGT reform could drive investment shift from property to shares, ABC analysis suggests
items.summary: ABC News analysis examining how the Budget's capital gains tax changes may redirect investor behaviour from residential property toward Australian shares. The analysis cites Treasury data showing inflation comprised 56% of ASX 200 share price growth over the decade to March 2026, arguing investors in shares have been 'undercompensated' by current CGT settings compared to property investors.

items.title: Guardian analysis: CGT concession benefits concentrated among top 1% of income earners
items.summary: The Guardian's analysis of Budget 2026 reveals that more than half of the capital gains tax discount benefit flows to the top 1% of income earners, based on the most recent available ATO data. The analysis includes interactive visualisations illustrating the distributional impact of CGT arrangements across income brackets. Researchers found the CGT discount disproportionately favours high-wealth individuals with property and share investments.

items.title: Pitcher Partners: Superannuation unchanged in Budget 2026 but broader tax reform ripple effects remain
items.summary: Accounting firm Pitcher Partners confirms no major superannuation measures were announced in Budget 2026, though the enacted Division 296 legislation will take effect from 1 July 2026 and continue to impact high-balance SMSF members. The analysis also examines broader tax reform context, noting that CGT changes and negative gearing modifications represent interconnected policy shifts affecting SMSF strategies.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expanded from July 2027
items.summary: Budget 2026 includes expansion of venture capital tax incentives effective from July 2027, with new details on eligibility criteria and investment thresholds. The measure aims to encourage greater private investment in early-stage Australian businesses. Taxpayers and fund managers should review the updated requirements to ensure compliance when the changes take effect.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis released with the Budget shows inflation comprised 56 per cent of asset price growth for ASX 200 shares held for 10 years to March 2026. The data provides empirical justification for the government's proposed capital gains tax indexation reforms, which would allow investors to adjust CGT for inflation. The analysis underscores the impact of inflationary pressures on long-term investment returns.

items.title: ASX analysis details CGT reform impact on ETF and Listed Investment Vehicle investors
items.summary: The ASX published an investor update analysing how the proposed CGT changes affect ETFs and Listed Investment Vehicles (LIVs), including practical implications for share market investors. The exchange's investor update examines how indexation and the 30% minimum tax floor apply to these investment vehicles, noting share market investors have been 'undercompensated' for inflation under current settings. This update provides essential guidance for investors navigating the proposed tax changes to capital gains.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expanded from July 2027 in budget measure
items.summary: The federal budget has expanded venture capital tax incentives, extending the program from 1 July 2027 as part of a broader tax reform package. The measure reflects the government's shift from taxing income to taxing assets, providing enhanced incentives for venture capital investment. This expansion aims to support innovation and growth in the startup ecosystem.

items.title: Foreign resident capital gains notification threshold remains at $50m
items.summary: The much-anticipated legislation to lower the foreign resident capital gains withholding notification threshold has been deferred again. The threshold will remain at $50 million for the foreseeable future, with the government confirming the changes will not proceed in this budget cycle. This comes despite earlier indications that the legislation would be introduced to target higher-value property transactions by foreign residents.

items.title: ATO confirms pre-1985 share valuation reset for 1 July 2027 CGT changes
items.summary: The ATO has released guidance confirming that investors holding shares acquired before 20 September 1985 can access a valuation reset to establish a new cost base ahead of the CGT discount reforms taking effect from 1 July 2027. This grandfathering arrangement allows legacy shareholders to potentially benefit from the new inflation-indexed cost base rules. Taxpayers should review their pre-1985 share holdings and consider obtaining independent valuations before the changes take effect.

items.title: ABC analysis: CGT changes could shift investment from property to shares
items.summary: The ABC reports that capital gains tax changes may redirect investment away from property toward shares. The current flat 50% discount is being replaced with inflation-based indexation and a minimum 30% tax on real gains from July 2027. Analysts suggest this reform could fundamentally alter investment behaviour across the property and share markets.

items.title: Federal Budget introduces significant reforms to negative gearing
items.summary: Accounting firm William Buck confirms negative gearing reforms restrict access to tax benefits from 1 July 2027 for established properties purchased after 7:30pm on budget night (12 May 2026). New builds will remain exempt from the changes, allowing investors in newly constructed properties to continue claiming negative gearing deductions as before.

items.title: ATO confirms Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details
items.summary: The ATO has officially published details on the Division 296 superannuation tax thresholds for 2026-27, including indexed thresholds and CGT relief provisions for affected taxpayers. Division 296 applies a 30% tax on superannuation balances exceeding $3 million, with indexation adjustments for the new financial year. The ATO guidance clarifies capital gains tax (CGT) relief mechanisms available to trustees who need to restructure holdings in response to the new tax arrangements.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 'two-speed' tax treatment for investors
items.summary: ASX analysis details how CGT indexation versus minimum tax floor will create different outcomes for assets held long-term versus short-term, with transitional rules for assets purchased before 1 July 2027. The interaction between inflation indexation and 30% minimum tax creates different effective tax rates depending on holding period and asset type, with particular implications for Listed Investment Companies and ETFs with embedded gains.

items.title: Australian Shareholders Association calls for capital gains averaging alongside indexation
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association has formally submitted to Treasury calling for a capital gains averaging mechanism to complement the proposed indexation reforms. The ASA warns that indexation alone fails to address income bunching, where multi-year gains realised in a single tax year create cumulative tax disadvantages for long-term investors. The submission argues that averaging would provide fairer treatment for investors who hold assets for extended periods before realisation.

items.title: Guardian analysis: CGT concession benefits concentrated among top 1% of income earners
items.summary: Guardian analysis of Treasury and ATO data reveals the capital gains tax discount disproportionately benefits the highest income earners, with the top 1% capturing a significant share of the $55 billion annual concession. The 50% discount primarily advantages top income earners, raising questions about whether proposed reforms adequately address inequality or simply shift the burden to other taxpayers. Analysts argue the current arrangements entrench wealth inequality and call for more fundamental restructuring of Australia's property tax settings.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 'two-speed' tax treatment for different investor types
items.summary: The ASX investor update special edition identifies that recent CGT changes create significantly different tax outcomes depending on asset type, with transitional rules and exemptions creating complexity for ETF and Listed Investment Vehicle (LIV) investors. The analysis highlights that investors holding different asset classes will face varying effective tax rates under the new arrangements, requiring careful planning to optimise tax positions.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expanded from July 2027 in Budget 2026 measure
items.summary: Budget 2026 includes expansion of venture capital tax incentives commencing from 1 July 2027, providing early policy direction for the startup ecosystem. The measure complements existing CGT and negative gearing changes with targeted support for innovation investment. This builds on Australia's venture capital tax incentive framework to encourage greater private investment in early-stage companies.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 'two-speed' tax treatment for investors
items.summary: ASX analysis identifies that CGT reforms create differential tax treatment between investors who bought before versus after budget night, with transitional rules creating distinct outcomes for property and share investors. Pre-budget investors will retain current CGT discount rules, while post-budget investors face a minimum 30% tax on inflation-adjusted gains from July 2027. The reform effectively creates a two-speed tax treatment that will significantly impact investment decisions going forward.

items.title: Guardian analysis: CGT concession benefits concentrated among top 1% of income earners
items.summary: The Guardian analysis finds that capital gains tax concessions disproportionately benefit the highest income earners in Australia. The CGT discount is concentrated among the top 1% of income earners, highlighting the unequal distribution of tax benefits under current arrangements. This analysis provides important context for the tax reforms being implemented in the 2026 budget.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform details confirmed — Government signals shift from income to asset taxation
items.summary: The government has confirmed plans to reform trust tax treatment, shifting the taxation burden from income to assets. This represents a third major tax reform pillar alongside the previously announced capital gains and negative gearing changes. Legislation remains pending as the government works to implement this comprehensive tax reform package.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 formally lodged
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has been formally lodged in Parliament, containing the Capital Gains Tax (CGT) indexation changes and negative gearing legislative reforms announced in the federal budget. The Bill is currently before the Senate and has been referred to the Economics References Committee for examination.

items.title: Superannuation unchanged in Budget 2026 but broader tax reform ripple effects remain
items.summary: While no major superannuation measures were announced in the 2026-27 Federal Budget, accounting firm Pitcher Partners highlights that the Division 296 legislation commencing 1 July 2026 and CGT changes will have significant ripple effects on self-managed super funds (SMSFs) and retirement planning strategies. SMSF trustees should review their investment structures and contribution strategies ahead of the upcoming legislative changes.

items.title: Guardian analysis: CGT concession benefits concentrated among top 1% of income earners
items.summary: Analysis reveals that capital gains tax concessions disproportionately benefit the highest income earners, with the top 1% capturing the majority of these tax advantages. The report provides important distributional context for the federal budget's proposed CGT reforms and their impact on income inequality.

items.title: NAB Budget Analysis: CGT discount replaced by cost base indexation — implications for investors
items.summary: National Australia Bank has published comprehensive analysis of the federal budget changes to capital gains tax treatment, replacing the 50% CGT discount with cost base indexation for assets held longer than 12 months. The analysis examines how this policy shift affects property investors, share traders, and business owners, outlining scenarios where the new indexed cost base method may be more or less favourable than the previous discount approach. NAB's economists also assess the broader market implications and recommend strategies for investors to adapt to the new CGT framework effective from 1 July 2026.

items.title: Government confirms new tax cuts for Australian workers alongside CGT reform
items.summary: Budget 2026-27 confirms new tax cuts for Australian workers as part of a broader tax reform package. The measures include replacement of the 50% CGT discount with inflation indexation and introduction of a minimum 30% tax on gains from 1 July 2027. Treasurer Jim Chalmers stated the reforms aim to rebalance the taxation system away from taxing incomes and more towards taxing assets.

items.title: ATO releases Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed the indexed thresholds for Division 296 tax and details of CGT relief for affected superannuation accounts. The $3 million threshold applies from 1 July 2026 per enacted legislation, with an additional 15% tax on earnings related to balances exceeding the levy surplus balance. Tax agents and SMSF trustees should review member balances ahead of the implementation date to assess potential exposure.

items.title: ABC Analysis: CGT changes could drive investment shift from property to shares
items.summary: ABC News analysis examines how the replacement of the flat 50% CGT discount with inflation indexation and a minimum 30% tax rate could redirect investment away from property towards shares from July 2027. The changes, part of the 2026 federal budget, fundamentally alter the tax treatment of capital gains for property and share investors. Market analysts suggest the reforms could level the playing field between asset classes, potentially reshaping investment portfolios across Australia.

items.title: Working Australians Tax Offset: $250 annual relief confirmed for workers
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget introduces a new Working Australians Tax Offset providing $250 annual relief for eligible workers. This measure forms part of the broader tax reform package that shifts the taxation burden from income to assets. The offset is designed to provide direct financial relief to working Australians while complementing other income tax reforms announced in the budget.

items.title: NAB revises housing forecast: brief correction not prolonged slump
items.summary: NAB has revised its housing forecast following the federal Budget, predicting a brief property market correction rather than a prolonged slump. The bank notes that negative gearing restrictions will only apply to established properties purchased after budget night, limiting the overall market impact. This suggests investor activity may stabilise sooner than initially feared.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expanded from July 2027 as part of Budget 2026 measures
items.summary: The Budget 2026-27 includes expansion of venture capital tax incentives, with changes commencing from 1 July 2027. The measures are designed to boost investment in early-stage Australian companies by providing enhanced tax benefits for eligible venture capital investments.

items.title: Division 296 CGT relief for SMSFs explained by Heffron
items.summary: Heffron analysis confirms draft legislation includes specific CGT relief provisions for self-managed superannuation funds transitioning under Division 296, with indexed thresholds and timing rules clarified ahead of 1 July 2026 commencement. This guidance helps SMSF trustees understand how to manage the tax implications of the new Division 296 provisions.

items.title: Working Australians Tax Offset details confirmed: $250 annual relief for workers
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget confirms a new Working Australians Tax Offset providing $250 annual relief for eligible workers. The offset forms part of a broader personal income tax reform package targeting low-to-middle income earners, alongside reforms to capital gains and negative gearing provisions.

items.title: ASA calls for capital gains averaging alongside indexation reform
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association has publicly called for any capital gains tax reform to include both indexation and a modern averaging mechanism to address income bunching, where many years of gains are realised in a single tax year. The ASA expressed concern about the lack of consultation with shareholder groups on proposed CGT changes. The group is pushing for comprehensive reform that recognises the long-term nature of shareholding and prevents punitive tax outcomes for investors who accumulate gains over extended periods.

items.title: ABC Analysis: CGT changes could drive investment shift from property to shares
items.summary: ABC News analysis of budget data reveals investors in the Australian share market have been undercompensated for inflation impact, with inflation accounting for 56% of asset price growth for ASX 200 shares held for 10 years. The analysis examines how proposed CGT changes could redirect investment flows from property to shares, potentially reshaping the Australian investment landscape.

items.title: ATO confirms Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details for SMSFs
items.summary: The ATO has published guidance confirming that Division 296 tax on superannuation balances above $3 million is now law. The guidance includes indexed thresholds and specific capital gains tax (CGT) relief provisions for self-managed super funds (SMSFs) transitioning before the 1 July 2026 commencement date. SMSF trustees should review their investment strategies and consider timing of any asset disposals in light of these provisions.

items.title: Guardian analysis: CGT concession benefits concentrated among top 1% of income earners
items.summary: Analysis reveals the capital gains tax discount disproportionately benefits the highest income earners, with the benefit flowing primarily to the top 1% of income earners rather than average Australians. The data highlights growing inequality in Australia's tax system as property investors and high-net-worth individuals capture the majority of CGT concession benefits. This analysis provides context for the policy rationale behind reform measures in the federal budget.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 'two-speed' tax treatment for different investor types
items.summary: The ASX analysis outlines how the new CGT rules create differential treatment between investors based on asset type, timing of purchase, and whether investments are in property versus shares/ETFs. The reforms create a complex two-speed taxation environment that will require investors to carefully consider the timing and structure of their investments. This development has significant implications for investment strategy going forward.

items.title: ABC analysis: CGT changes could drive investment shift from property to shares
items.summary: The ABC reports that capital gains tax changes announced in the budget may cause investors to shift portfolio allocation away from residential property investment towards share market investments. This potential redirection could reshape residential property demand dynamics, with implications for both housing markets and share market activity.

items.title: ABC analysis: CGT changes could drive investment shift from property to shares
items.summary: Replacing the flat 50% CGT discount with inflation-aligned indexation and a minimum 30% tax on real gains from July 2027 may shift investor behaviour from property towards shares and ETFs. The analysis examines how these capital gains tax reforms could redirect investment away from residential property. Property investors may face increased tax burdens compared to those investing in shares and ETFs under the new regime.

items.title: 50% CGT discount replaced by cost base indexation
items.summary: The 50% CGT discount is being replaced by cost base indexation as part of the biggest personal tax changes in decades. Individual and investment taxpayers should review asset holding periods to understand the implications for their tax positions. This fundamental shift in capital gains taxation affects how gains are calculated for assets held beyond 12 months.

items.title: NAB revises housing forecast: brief correction not prolonged slump
items.summary: NAB has revised its housing price forecast following the 2026 Budget, predicting a brief correction rather than a prolonged slump. The bank's updated outlook suggests that proposed changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax will have a limited impact on property values. The revised forecast indicates market stability is expected to return relatively quickly despite initial headwinds from policy changes.

items.title: Budget allocates $47.5 million for CGT reform implementation
items.summary: The government will provide $47.5 million over four years from 2026–27, along with $3.9 million per year on an ongoing basis, to the Treasury and the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) to implement the CGT reform changes. This funding will support the administrative and technical requirements necessary for implementing the proposed capital gains tax reforms. The investment reflects the complexity of implementing significant CGT policy changes across the tax system.

items.title: ASX analysis reveals 'two-speed' CGT treatment for different investor types under reform package
items.summary: ASX analysis details how CGT reforms create differential outcomes across investor types: SMSFs retain the one-third discount on superannuation assets, listed investment vehicles face modified treatment, while direct share investors move to indexation-based cost bases. The analysis quantifies impacts across ETF, Listed Investment Company (LIC), and Listed Investment Trust (LIT) structures, highlighting the complexity of the tiered treatment approach.

items.title: ATO confirms Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details
items.summary: The ATO has released comprehensive guidance on Division 296 tax calculation methods, confirming the indexed thresholds for the 2026–27 financial year. The guidance includes detailed information on CGT relief provisions available to affected superannuation funds, particularly those with total superannuation balances approaching the $1.9 million transfer balance cap. SMSF trustees and administrators should review the guidance to ensure compliance with the new requirements.

items.title: ASA calls for capital gains averaging mechanism alongside indexation reform
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association has formally called on the Government to incorporate a capital gains averaging mechanism into the CGT reform package. The ASA argues that indexation alone fails to address income bunching, where gains accrued over many years are realised in a single tax year, potentially pushing investors into higher tax brackets. The peak body warns that the current reform proposal does not adequately address the concerns of investors who accumulate gains over extended holding periods.

items.title: SMSF property confirmed exempt from negative gearing changes
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget confirms that self-managed superannuation fund property investments retain their current tax treatment and are not subject to negative gearing restrictions. SMSF trustees can continue to use gearing strategies within their super fund without the limitations applied to residential property investors. This maintains the existing framework for SMSF property investment while new build restrictions apply separately to personal residential investors.

items.title: Parliamentary committee endorsed CGT discount changes in March 2026
items.summary: A parliamentary committee endorsed changes to the capital gains tax discount before the budget was handed down, providing important context for the 2026 budget CGT reforms. The Liberal Party opposed the changes but was unable to block the referral, as crossbench support ensured the proposal moved forward. This committee endorsement set the stage for the broader tax changes announced in the May 2026 federal budget.

items.title: Budget housing measures cost $6.4 billion over four years — ABC confirms official costing for negative gearing and CGT reform package
items.summary: The ABC's Budget winners and losers analysis reveals the first official costing figure for the government's housing measures package at $6.4 billion over four years. The comprehensive package includes changes to negative gearing rules, capital gains tax reforms, and related housing initiatives designed to improve housing affordability. This figure represents the net cost to the budget of the full suite of housing policy changes announced in the Budget.

items.title: Federal Budget 2026: $1,000 Instant Tax Deduction for Work-Related Expenses Confirmed
items.summary: The 2026 Federal Budget has confirmed a new $1,000 instant tax deduction for work-related expenses, effective from the current financial year. This measure is separate from the Working Australians Tax Offset (WATSO) which provides $250 relief, offering a distinct tax benefit for eligible workers claiming work-related deductions. The instant deduction simplifies tax time by allowing individuals to claim the flat $1,000 amount without needing to itemise specific expenses.

items.title: ASA calls for capital gains averaging alongside indexation to address 'income bunching'
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association has welcomed the government's move to index capital gains tax but warns it does not fully address income bunching, where investors may realise decades of gains in a single tax year. The ASA is calling for any CGT reform to incorporate a modern averaging mechanism alongside indexation, arguing this would provide fairer treatment for long-term investors. The group also expressed concern about the lack of proper consultation before such significant changes were announced.

items.title: Division 296: ATO confirms indexed thresholds for Better Targeted Super Concessions
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed that the Better Targeted Super Concessions legislation (Division 296) will commence on 1 July 2026 with indexed thresholds. The $3 million total superannuation balance threshold will be indexed to CPI annually, ensuring the tax only impacts those with substantial superannuation balances. SMSF members approaching the threshold should review their contribution strategies and account structures before the changes take effect.

items.title: CGT relief confirmed for SMSFs affected by Division 296 tax changes
items.summary: The ATO has outlined the Capital Gains Tax (CGT) relief available for SMSFs affected by the Division 296 tax on superannuation balances exceeding $3 million. Affected funds can choose to reset the cost base of certain assets and trigger a CGT event before 1 July 2026 to manage their exposure to the new tax. Trustees should seek professional advice to determine whether exercising this relief is appropriate for their circumstances.

items.title: KPMG confirms $47.5m implementation funding for CGT and negative gearing reforms
items.summary: KPMG has confirmed the Federal Budget 2026/27 allocates $47.5 million over four years from 2026-27 (and $3.9 million per year ongoing) to Treasury and ATO for implementation of CGT reform and negative gearing changes. This funding will support the administrative requirements and systems updates needed to operationalise the proposed property tax reforms. The investment represents the government's commitment to implementing these significant housing tax policy changes.

items.title: Working Australians Tax Offset: $250 annual relief confirmed for low-to-middle income workers
items.summary: The 2026 Budget introduces a new Working Australians Tax Offset providing $250 annual relief for low-to-middle income workers. This measure forms part of the government's broader tax reform package alongside changes to capital gains tax and negative gearing policies. Eligible workers will receive the offset when lodging their tax returns, with the relief designed to assist those earning above the tax-free threshold but below higher income brackets.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 'two-speed' tax treatment for ETF and Listed Investment Vehicle investors
items.summary: The ASX published investor-focused analysis explaining how the Capital Gains Tax changes affect different investor types differently. The analysis highlights that exchange-traded funds and listed investment vehicles now face a different tax treatment compared to direct share investors, creating what the ASX describes as a 'two-speed' tax environment under the reform package. Investors holding ETFs and listed vehicles should review their portfolio tax positions in light of these differential treatment implications.

items.title: ABC Budget 2026: Winners and losers — $6.4 billion housing measure cost confirmed
items.summary: ABC News analysis confirms the housing measures announced in Budget 2026 cost $6.4 billion over four years. The report also notes the $1,000 instant tax deduction for work-related expenses as confirmed from pre-election announcements. The analysis provides a comprehensive breakdown of which Australians benefit most from the government's spending priorities.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expansion confirmed from July 2027
items.summary: Budget 2026 has confirmed the expansion of venture capital tax incentives from 1 July 2027 as part of broader innovation and investment support measures. The expansion aims to strengthen Australia's venture capital sector and encourage more private investment in early-stage companies. This measure builds on previous government initiatives to support startup growth and economic diversification.

items.title: ASX analysis details CGT reform impact on ETF and Listed Investment Vehicle investors
items.summary: The ASX Investor Update examines how proposed capital gains tax changes create a 'two-speed' tax treatment for Australian share market investors. Exchange-traded funds and Listed Investment Vehicles face different tax outcomes compared to direct share ownership under the proposed reforms. Investors holding these structures should review how the changes affect their portfolio strategy and tax position.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform details confirmed — Government signals shift from income to asset taxation
items.summary: The Government has confirmed plans to reform trust tax treatment as part of broader reforms to shift the taxation burden from income to assets. Treasurer Jim Chalmers indicated the plan will 'rebalance the system' away from taxing incomes and more toward taxing assets, with trust taxation changes flagged alongside CGT and negative gearing reforms. This represents a significant policy shift in the federal budget approach to taxation.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 22 percentage point tax increase for low-rate retirees
items.summary: An ASX investor analysis highlights how proposed capital gains tax changes would significantly impact retirees with long-held equity portfolios. An investor on a 16% marginal tax rate currently faces an effective 8% tax on nominal gains, but under the proposed indexed gains approach this would rise to 30%. The analysis provides specific comparison scenarios showing how different investor types would be affected by the CGT reforms announced in the 2026 Federal Budget.

items.title: Budget confirms trust tax treatment reform as core part of asset taxation shift
items.summary: The federal budget has confirmed that trust tax treatment reform will be a core component of the government's asset taxation overhaul. The changes, which also include capital gains tax adjustments and negative gearing modifications, form part of a broader plan to rebalance the tax system 'away from taxing incomes and more towards taxing assets'. Budget.gov.au has explicitly listed the trust tax changes alongside these other measures as central to the reform package.

items.title: Budget housing measures cost $6.4 billion over four years — ABC analysis confirms official costing
items.summary: ABC analysis has confirmed the official costing of the Albanese government's housing package, which includes negative gearing and capital gains tax reforms, at $6.4 billion over four years. The analysis identifies winners and losers from the budget measures, examining impacts on property investors, first-home buyers, and the broader housing market.

items.title: Guardian analysis shows CGT concession benefits concentrated among top 1% of income earners — data reveals distributional impact of current arrangements
items.summary: The Guardian's analysis of the most recent tax data reveals that more than half of the benefit from the capital gains tax (CGT) concession flowed to the top 1% of income earners in Australia. This distributional finding highlights the significant wealth concentration inherent in current CGT arrangements and provides key context for ongoing tax reform debates in the 2026 federal budget. The analysis forms part of a broader examination of how tax settings on property and investment assets disproportionately benefit higher-income households.

items.title: ATO confirms Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) is law — 15% tax applies from 1 July 2026 on earnings above threshold
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed that the Better Targeted Super Concessions legislation (Division 296) is now law. From 1 July 2026, individuals with a total superannuation balance exceeding the lower threshold will face a 15% tax on earnings relating to the portion of their balance above that threshold. The ATO has published official guidance confirming the implementation timing and details for affected individuals.

items.title: Division 296 draft legislation released with CGT relief provisions
items.summary: Treasury has released Division 296 draft legislation with detailed guidance on indexed thresholds, CGT relief provisions, and SMSF-specific rules. Heffron SMSF specialists have analysed the legislation confirming key compliance requirements and calculation methodologies. SMSF trustees should review their current holdings and update their accounting systems before the 1 July 2026 commencement date.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform details confirmed
items.summary: The government has confirmed details on trust tax treatment reform, signalling a shift from taxing income to taxing assets. The Treasurer has stated the goal of 'rebalancing the system, away from taxing incomes and more towards taxing assets'. The reform package includes changes to how trusts are taxed alongside the CGT and negative gearing reforms.

items.title: ATO confirms pre-1985 share valuation reset for 1 July 2027
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed that pre-1985 share holdings will receive a valuation reset as part of the CGT reform package taking effect from 1 July 2027. This provision allows historical assets to use a new cost base assessment date, addressing concerns about compounding inflation on long-held assets acquired before 1985. Taxpayers with pre-1985 share holdings should review their CGT position and consider the impact of this reset on their tax obligations.

items.title: Division 296 CGT relief for SMSFs confirmed
items.summary: The ATO has released detailed guidance on CGT relief provisions available to SMSFs affected by Division 296 tax changes. The relief applies when SMSF members exceed the $3m total superannuation balance threshold, providing relief from double taxation scenarios. The guidance includes indexed thresholds and specific conditions that must be met to claim the relief.

items.title: Treasury analysis: Inflation accounted for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury and ABS data reveals inflation comprised 56% of total ASX 200 returns over the 10 years to March 2026, accounting for the majority of asset price growth. The analysis provides a quantitative foundation for proposed indexation reforms affecting capital gains tax and investment policy. The findings support arguments that nominal returns overstate actual investment performance when adjusted for purchasing power erosion.

items.title: Budget confirms inflation-indexed CGT discount from July 2027
items.summary: The official Budget.gov.au tax reform page confirms the 50% CGT discount will be replaced by an inflation-indexed discount from 1 July 2027. A minimum 30% tax will apply to capital gains under the new framework, replacing the current flat 50% discount. This represents a fundamental shift in how capital gains are taxed in Australia.

items.title: ATO confirms Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) is law — 15% tax applies from 1 July 2026 on earnings above $3m threshold
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed that Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) legislation has been enacted and will apply from 1 July 2026. The new law introduces a 15% tax on superannuation earnings relating to total superannuation balances exceeding the $3 million low-balance threshold. Individuals affected should review their SMSF investment strategies and retirement planning in light of this change.

items.title: SMSFs confirmed exempt — retain one-third CGT discount under new indexation-based rules
items.summary: Self-managed superannuation funds (SMSFs) with property assets will retain the one-third CGT discount under the new Division 296 regime commencing 1 July 2027. This distinguishes SMSFs from standard individual investors who face transition from the existing 50% discount to inflation-adjusted cost base calculations. SMSF trustees should continue applying the one-third discount when calculating capital gains for assets disposed after the commencement date.

items.title: ATO confirms Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) is law
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed that Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) legislation has been enacted. From 1 July 2026, a 15% tax will apply on earnings relating to total superannuation balances exceeding the $3 million threshold. The ATO has also confirmed indexed thresholds and CGT relief provisions for SMSFs in relation to this measure.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expanded from July 2027
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget confirms the expansion of venture capital tax incentives, effective 1 July 2027. These measures extend tax benefits for venture capital investments as part of broader innovation and investment policy reforms. Businesses and investors should review how these changes may impact their investment strategies and tax planning.

items.title: Parliamentary committee endorsed CGT discount changes
items.summary: A parliamentary committee endorsed changes to the capital gains tax (CGT) discount on 17 March 2026, several months before the reforms were officially tabled in the May 2026 budget. The endorsement marked an early step in the government's planned CGT reforms, setting the stage for the formal budget announcement on 12 May 2026.

items.title: ASX analysis quantifies CGT impact: retired investor on 16% marginal rate faces 8% vs 30% effective tax rate on long-held equity gains
items.summary: ASX analysis reveals that a retired investor on a 16% marginal tax rate currently faces only 8% effective tax on nominal gains from a long-held equity portfolio. Under proposed CGT changes, this same investor would face a 30% effective rate on indexed gains. This analysis demonstrates the significant impact of the reform on lower-income retirees who depend on equity investments for retirement income.

items.title: ASX analysis quantifies retirement investor tax increase under CGT reforms
items.summary: An ASX analysis provides concrete numerical examples of how the proposed inflation-indexed capital gains tax system would affect retired investors. A retiree on a 16% marginal tax rate currently faces an effective 8% tax on nominal capital gains, but would face 30% tax on inflation-indexed gains under the proposed changes — representing a 22 percentage point increase. The analysis highlights the significant impact on retirement investors who rely on equity investments for income.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 22 percentage point tax increase for low-rate retirees
items.summary: ASX analysis quantifies the impact of proposed CGT changes on retirees. A retired investor on a 16% marginal tax rate faces an effective tax rate increase from 8% to 30% on long-held equity gains under the new rules. The analysis highlights the significant impact of the minimum 30% tax floor on low-rate taxpayers, demonstrating how the reform disproportionately affects those in lower tax brackets.

items.title: ASA calls for capital gains averaging alongside indexation to address income bunching
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association is calling for a capital gains averaging mechanism to be introduced alongside the inflation indexation reform. ASA argues that the current reform does not address 'income bunching' where many years of gains are realised in a single tax year, and that proper consultation should have occurred before major changes were announced. The association believes that averaging would provide more equitable treatment for investors who hold assets for extended periods.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform signals shift from income to asset taxation
items.summary: The 2026 Budget flags significant reforms to trust tax treatment as part of the broader shift from taxing incomes to taxing assets. The reforms aim to move away from taxing incomes and more towards taxing assets, with trust structures likely to face changes to their tax treatment. This includes potential changes to how distributions from trusts are taxed, which could affect partnership and trust structures.

items.title: Treasury analysis: Inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Budget documentation shows that inflation made up 56% of asset price growth for ASX 200 shares held for 10 years to March 2026. The analysis underpins the Government's rationale for replacing the CGT discount with inflation indexation, as investors in the share market have been 'undercompensated' for the impact of inflation by the current CGT settings.

items.title: Division 296: CGT relief confirmed for SMSFs affected by high-balance super tax
items.summary: Treasury has released draft legislation for Division 296 including specific CGT relief provisions for self-managed super funds. The legislation provides indexed thresholds, transitional rules, and provisions to prevent double taxation for SMSFs with balances exceeding $3 million, with implementation scheduled for 1 July 2026.

items.title: ASX analysis quantifies CGT reform impact on retirement investors — 8% vs 30% effective rate
items.summary: An ASX analysis provides specific numbers showing that a retired investor on a 16% marginal rate currently pays 8% tax on nominal gains from long-held equities, but would face 30% tax on indexed gains under the announced CGT changes. This creates a 22 percentage point tax increase for this investor type, significantly affecting retirees with substantial equity portfolios held over many years.

items.title: Government signals broader trust tax treatment reform as part of asset taxation shift
items.summary: The Government has signaled plans to shift taxation burden from income to assets, with changes to trust structures expected as part of a broader tax reform package. Reform to trust tax treatment is flagged as a core component of Budget 2026, working alongside changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax. The measures are intended to rebalance the taxation system and are detailed in the Guardian's explanation of the 2026 federal budget tax reforms.

items.title: ASX analysis quantifies CGT reform impact on retirement investors
items.summary: ASX analysis provides a concrete numerical example showing the effective tax rate increase for a retired investor on a 16% marginal tax rate: from 8% on nominal gains under current rules to 30% on indexed gains under the proposed changes, representing a 22 percentage point increase. The analysis illustrates how the shift from nominal to indexed capital gains calculations significantly impacts retired investors relying on investment income.

items.title: ABC Budget 2026: Winners and losers — $6.4 billion housing measure cost confirmed
items.summary: ABC News reports the official costing of the housing package containing negative gearing and CGT changes at $6.4 billion over four years. The analysis examines distributional impacts, identifying which groups benefit and which face losses from the reforms. This represents a significant confirmation of the government's major housing policy direction.

items.title: ASA calls for capital gains averaging alongside indexation to address income bunching
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association has urged the government to introduce a capital gains averaging mechanism alongside the inflation indexation reform to prevent 'income bunching'. The ASA warns that without averaging, gains realised in a single year can push taxpayers into higher marginal tax brackets, creating unfair outcomes. The association is calling for proper consultation before major changes to capital gains tax rules are announced.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027
items.summary: The ATO has published comprehensive guidance on how inflation indexation will be calculated under the new capital gains tax (CGT) rules taking effect from 1 July 2027. The guidance includes detailed cost base adjustment methodologies and worked examples covering different asset classes including shares, property, and managed funds. Tax practitioners and SMSF trustees are encouraged to review the guidance to ensure proper application of the indexation factors when calculating CGT obligations.

items.title: KPMG analysis: Implementation timeline risks as ATO prepares for CGT reform with $47.5m funding
items.summary: KPMG's Federal Budget analysis highlights significant implementation challenges for the ATO and Treasury in delivering proposed CGT and negative gearing changes by the planned July 2027 commencement date. The government has allocated $47.5 million over four years to fund necessary system updates, IT infrastructure changes, and development of compliance guidance materials. KPMG notes that the tight timeline creates execution risks that could impact the effectiveness of these major tax reforms.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 formally lodged with Parliament
items.summary: The government has formally introduced enabling legislation codifying changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax. The Bill specifies the 7:30pm Budget Night cutoff for restrictions on established properties, confirms new builds remain exempt, and establishes the inflation-indexed CGT discount replacing the existing 50% discount from 1 July 2027. The legislation is currently before the Senate with debate timeline now publicly documented.

items.title: NAB revises housing forecast following Budget tax reforms
items.summary: National Australia Bank economists have revised their property market outlook following Budget night tax changes. The analysis projects a brief correction in established property prices rather than a prolonged slump, with limited market impact attributed to grandfathering provisions and new build exemptions softening the adjustment. The short-term outlook is more optimistic than earlier projections.

items.title: Parliamentary committee endorsed CGT discount changes on 17 March 2026
items.summary: A parliamentary committee formally endorsed changes to the capital gains tax discount on 17 March 2026, prior to the Budget announcement. This endorsement represents an important milestone in the legislative process for the proposed CGT reform. The timing provides valuable context for understanding when the reform proposal gained parliamentary support ahead of the May Budget.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027
items.summary: The ATO has released comprehensive guidance to help investors and tax professionals navigate the new capital gains tax indexation rules taking effect on 1 July 2027. The guidance provides detailed instructions for calculating indexed cost bases, including worked examples and scenarios applicable to various asset types. Tax practitioners are encouraged to review the materials to ensure compliance when the new rules commence.

items.title: KPMG flags implementation timeline risks as ATO prepares for CGT reform
items.summary: KPMG analysis has identified potential challenges with the ATO's implementation timeline for the CGT indexation changes. The firm notes the government's $47.5 million funding allocation for Treasury and ATO to implement the reform, while highlighting risks around system updates, guidance development, and compliance with the proposed changes. The analysis suggests stakeholders should monitor implementation readiness as the July 1 commencement date approaches.

items.title: ASA calls for capital gains averaging mechanism alongside indexation
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association is urging the Government to introduce a capital gains averaging mechanism to address 'income bunching' where gains realised in a single tax year could push taxpayers into higher brackets. The ASA argues that such a mechanism would complement the existing indexation method for capital gains, providing a more equitable approach to taxing investment returns. This proposal comes as part of the ASA's pre-budget submission for the 2026-27 federal budget cycle.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 formally lodged with Parliament
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has been formally lodged with Parliament, containing the negative gearing restrictions and capital gains tax reform measures announced in the 2026-27 Budget. The bill will now face Senate scrutiny as part of the legislative process to implement key housing affordability measures. Taxpayers and property investors should monitor the bill's progress through Parliament as these reforms will significantly impact property investment strategies.

items.title: ATO releases Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details for SMSFs
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed indexed thresholds for the Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) tax that applies from 1 July 2026. The 15% additional tax applies on super earnings above the $3 million threshold, with thresholds indexed annually. CGT relief provisions have also been confirmed for SMSFs affected by the high-balance super tax.

items.title: NAB revises housing forecast following Budget tax reforms — brief correction not prolonged slump
items.summary: NAB has revised its housing forecast following the Budget tax reforms, projecting a brief correction rather than a prolonged property market slump. The bank expects the recent policy changes to have a limited negative impact on property prices, with any market adjustment expected to be short-lived. This suggests underlying demand remains resilient despite the tax reform uncertainties.

items.title: ASA calls for capital gains averaging alongside indexation to address income bunching
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association (ASA) has called on the Government to implement capital gains averaging alongside the existing indexation reform. The proposal aims to prevent 'income bunching' where multi-year gains realised in a single tax year could push investors into higher tax brackets. ASA argues that both mechanisms working together would create a fairer tax treatment for long-term investors.

items.title: KPMG flags implementation timeline risks as ATO prepares for CGT reform
items.summary: KPMG analysis highlights significant implementation challenges for the CGT indexation changes, noting the $47.5 million funding allocation and potential risks to the July 2027 commencement date given the complexity of transitioning systems and guidance. Industry stakeholders are urged to monitor implementation progress closely as the commencement date approaches.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027
items.summary: The ATO has published technical guidance to help investors calculate capital gains using the new inflation-indexation method, which will apply from 1 July 2027. items.title: NAB revises housing forecast following Budget tax reforms
items.summary: NAB has revised its housing market forecast in response to the Budget's negative gearing and capital gains tax changes, projecting a brief correction rather than a prolonged slump. The bank's updated analysis suggests the property market will experience a short-term adjustment period before stabilising. This revision indicates the major lender believes the tax reforms will have a limited long-term impact on housing demand.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027
items.summary: The Australian Taxation Office has released practical guidance for taxpayers calculating CGT indexation under the new rules commencing 1 July 2027. The guidance addresses how to apply the inflation-based cost base adjustments, helping investors and SMSFs prepare for the transition away from the 50% CGT discount. Taxpayers holding assets acquired after 1 July 2025 should review the guidance to ensure accurate calculations when the new indexation method takes effect.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 22 percentage point tax increase for low-rate retirees
items.summary: ASX analysis quantifies the impact of CGT reform on retirement investors. items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 formally lodged with Parliament
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has been formally lodged with Parliament, containing the legislative framework for the Budget's negative gearing and CGT reforms. items.title: Budget confirms $250 Working Australians Tax Offset annual relief for low-to-middle income workers
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget confirms a new $250 annual Working Australians Tax Offset providing targeted relief for low-to-middle income workers. This measure is separate from the broader CGT and negative gearing housing tax reforms also announced in the budget. The offset aims to ease cost-of-living pressures while maintaining work incentives for Australians earning below the tax-free threshold.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027
items.summary: The ATO has released practical guidance to help taxpayers calculate CGT indexation under the new rules effective 1 July 2027. This guidance helps investors and their advisors prepare for the transition from the 50% discount to inflation-based indexation. The ATO's practical guidance includes worked examples and calculators to assist with the transition.

items.title: ATO confirms pre-1985 share valuation reset for 1 July 2027 CGT changes
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed the valuation methodology for pre-1985 share holdings as part of the broader CGT reform package. items.summary: Treasury has released draft legislation for Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) including indexed thresholds, CGT relief provisions, and specific rules for self-managed super funds. items.summary: The Opposition Leader has indicated willingness to consider Senate inquiries and potential challenges to the Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026.
